title: Isolate long-context flows with prefetch quarantine to stop cross-tenant starvation
creator: Marco Chen
description:
Summary: A large enterprise customer escalated repeated production regressions where their short interactive requests experienced 10-100x latency spikes during multi-hour windowed bursts. Investigation shows a coupled interaction between the continuous batcher admission window, our prefetch/KV-warmup handshake, and the adaptive admission reservoir that allowed long-context flows to hold admission tokens and cause small-request starvation across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. This ticket implements a targeted isolation strategy ("prefetch quarantine") plus admission-smoothing guardrails to prevent long-context or prefetch-heavy requests from starving latency-sensitive flows without sacrificing overall throughput.

Repro/Observations:
- Repro in staging with mixed-length synthetic workload using the customer's token distributions; short requests (<=64 tokens) had median 12ms normally but saw spikes to 1.2s under mixed bursts.
- Traces show long-context flows take prefetch path and claim multiple admission slots while they warm KV cache; continuous batcher prioritizes throughput and leaves small requests behind in ingress queue.
- Dedicated hosts with tuned autoscaling exhibit same effect; private installs replicate when prefetch sampling is enabled.
- Correlated alerts: queue-depth surge + KV eviction churn during the same windows.

Root cause hypothesis: The scheduler's admission accounting treats prefetch + first-generation as single admission work unit and rewards it with continuous batching windows; prefetch handshake extends effective admission duration, and the admission reservoir has no per-tenant short-request protection. Under mixed workloads, a small number of concurrent long-context flows dominate admission tokens, producing queue starvation for short requests and amplifying tail latency.

Proposed fix (Prefetch Quarantine + Admission Smoothing):
1) Introduce a quarantine lane for requests that perform KV-prefetch or declare long expected context length at ingress. Requests in quarantine are admitted into dedicated "prefetch-sub-batches" with bounded concurrency (configurable per-tenant).
2) Add a short-request fastlane: identify requests with estimated output tokens <= 128 and prioritize admission windows using a lightweight fingerprint in ingress that does not touch model weights.
3) Admission smoothing: cap per-tenant admission tokens for prefetch-heavy flows and implement token leak rate to return unused prefetch capacity back to the shared pool faster.
4) Memory/eviction protections: enforce soft limits on prefetch KV footprint and fall back to on-demand prefetch for tenants approaching eviction thresholds.
5) Configuration: default enabled for hosted, opt-in for Dedicated/Private with a telemetry flag; conservative defaults for private installs to avoid behavior changes without operator approval.

Success criteria:
- Repro test in staging shows short-request p99 latency reduced from >800ms to <60ms under the same mixed workload.
- No throughput regression (>5% token/sec) for large-context workloads in the 24h regression window.
- No increase in KV eviction rate >10% above baseline.
- Canary in hosted for 1% traffic for 48h with no customer escalations.

Rollout plan:
- Merge feature-flagged implementation behind runtime-1.20 toggle.
- Unit + integration tests in CI with synthetic mixed workloads.
- Staging canary running deterministic replay for 72h.
- Hosted 1% -> 10% -> 50% stable rollout with dashboards.
- Dedicated/private: deliver as opt-in config and provide operator runbook for toggling.

Mitigations (short-term):
- Emergency knob: reduce admission window for all prefetched requests to 50% of default.
- Customer-specific workaround: tenant-level admission cap and explicit prefetch-disable for the customer.

Notes/Tradeoffs:
- Quarantine reduces mixing efficiency, may slightly reduce peak throughput for some long-only workloads. We expect gain in tail latency for interactive flows is worth the tradeoff for most customers.
- Private installs with strict change controls will require operator consent; provide a compatibility shim to revert to current behavior.

Artifacts: Confluence design doc and performance spreadsheets linked below.
